Before I learned about my eating disorder*, I was convinced that I was just allergic to foods (which is why I kept vomiting when I ate them). I started cutting them out and ended up gluten-free vegan. I went to my obese doctor and she asked about my diet. "I don't eat animal products or wheat gluten," I replied. "It's the same as before, but minus the wheat gluten."

Her mouth fell open, pushing back her cheek fat. "SO WHAT DO YOU EAT?!"

"Everything that isn't animals or wheat."

Her face was blank. It was as if this woman never knew about fruits, vegetables, nuts, or legumes. Her eyebrows begged for more information.

"I eat things like fruits, vegetables, nuts, and legumes. For example, I made burritos yesterday with avocado, black beans, squash, tomatoes, and rolled it up in a rice-flour tortilla."

Hams always have the same look when they hear about food. Their eyes glaze over and their gaze goes up a little as they dream about that food being in between their hooves as they shovel it down their gullet. "Ooooh, yum, that sounds great. What else?"

It struck me as odd. She seemed to not be interested in my meal plan as much as she was interested in specific foods about which to fantasize. This was verbal food porn for her. It's like we were two teenagers and I had just seen a real-life naked body the other teen desperately wanted me to describe. "Well, if you are worried about what I eat," I said, knowing she didn't really care about it from a health perspective, "I post all my recipes onto a blog." I typed it into her computer and she spent the rest of my visit looking at food and saying nothing.

Let me repeat that: I came to see my doctor for a routine physical as required by the veteran's hospital, and instead of her actually checking anything she just stared at food on the computer.
